questions.q: A team deploys a change set containing a Custom Setting's definition from sandbox to production. What happens to the Custom Setting's existing record values?
options: They deploy along with the definition automatically
They are left behind in the target org — only the definition deploys, not the data
They are merged with production's existing values field by field
The deployment fails unless the values match exactly
questions.explain: Custom Settings data does not travel with a deployment — the setting's definition deploys, but its records are left behind in the target org.

questions.q: Which configuration mechanism is the right fit for an integration endpoint mapping that must be identical across environments and promoted through a controlled release, same as code?
options: A Hierarchy Custom Setting
A List Custom Setting
A Custom Metadata Type
A standard custom object with no sharing rules
questions.explain: Custom Metadata Type records are packaged and deployable via change sets, the Metadata API, and packages — the right fit for configuration that should move identically between environments as part of a release.

questions.q: An on-call admin needs to flip an 'emergency bypass' flag directly in production during an incident, with no deployment window available. Which mechanism supports this, and why?
options: Custom Metadata Type, because its values can be queried quickly
Custom Setting, because its values can be changed directly via Apex DML in the org without a deployment cycle
Either works identically for this purpose
Neither — this requires a Big Object
questions.explain: Custom Settings are built for values changed directly in an org (including via Apex DML) without needing a deployment, which is exactly what an in-production emergency bypass requires.

questions.q: What is true about querying Custom Metadata Type records with SOQL, compared to querying standard or custom object records?
options: Custom Metadata queries are slower because they must resolve through the Metadata API
Custom Metadata queries count double against the SOQL governor limit
Queries against Custom Metadata records are not counted against the org's SOQL query governor limits
Custom Metadata Types cannot be queried with SOQL at all
questions.explain: Queries against Custom Metadata Type records are not counted toward the org's SOQL query governor limits, unlike ordinary object queries.

questions.q: A Hierarchy Custom Setting defines an org-wide default discount percentage, with an override for the 'Enterprise Sales' profile. A user on that profile runs code that reads the setting. What value resolves?
options: The org-wide default always wins regardless of profile overrides
Both values are returned and the code must pick one manually
The profile-level override resolves automatically, since Hierarchy settings cascade from org default down to profile/user overrides
The setting throws an error because two values exist for the same field
questions.explain: Hierarchy Custom Settings resolve automatically by cascading from the org-wide default down through profile and user-level overrides, so the most specific applicable override — here, the profile override — is what's returned.
